$comment: Auth settings this project holds deliberately, as code. Everything else
in the Auth config is left to Supabase's defaults and is never touched
by the apply job — a file claiming every field would go stale the first
Why this file exists: rate_limit_email_sent sat at 2 for months. Two auth
emails per hour, shared between sign-up and password recovery, was the
real reason recovery mail 'went missing' while /recover answered 200. It
was written off as a platform limit needing custom SMTP. It is a field in
the Auth config, and it stayed invisible because nothing in the repository
Every setting below carries a $<name> line saying why it holds that value;
a test fails if one is missing. Change a value, open a PR, then run the
Supabase Guardrails workflow with apply=true. The nightly run fails when
$mailer_otp_exp: 24 hours. A one-hour link expired before people opened their mail: six of seven password sign-ups never confirmed.
$mailer_autoconfirm: Addresses must be proven — certificates carry a person's name and are publicly verifiable.
$password_min_length: Server-side floor. The client asks for the same and shows the requirement; before 2026-08-31 it asked for 6 and the server refused at 12.
$password_hibp_enabled: Refuse passwords found in breach corpora. Free, and the audience reuses passwords.
$rate_limit_email_sent: Was 2/hour across sign-up and recovery: one teacher inviting a class, or one person retrying a reset, exhausted it and the next caller got a silent 200. Mail leaves through the send-email hook into Resend, whose limits are the real ceiling; 30/hour is generous here and far below them.
$refresh_token_rotation_enabled: A refresh token is spent on use, so a stolen one dies at the next legitimate refresh.
$security_refresh_token_reuse_interval: 10s grace so two requests firing at once do not log someone out; long enough for a slow mobile round trip, short enough to stay a grace window.
